text_narrative: Teodora carried the balloon out at ten to six, both arms under it, and the wind took the skin against her chin before she reached the launch square. The sonde swung on its cord and knocked her knee twice. She waited for the gust to pass, counted, and let go a little too early — the balloon went up sideways and the cord snapped taut against the mast.
text_nonnarrative: A failed launch is a matter of ascent angle, not of damage. Sideways ascent, meaning departure from vertical beyond thirty degrees, is one class of failure; contact between the cord and the mast is a second, independent of the first. Neither concerns the sonde. Wind speed at the square is the usual cause of both, and the gust interval, not the balloon or the skin, sets the margin.

text_narrative: The lamp had been unattended for eleven weeks when Salla climbed to the gallery and found the lens turning. It turned at the proper rate, four revolutions to the minute, and the clockwork beneath it was seized solid with rust. She put her hand on the drive weight. The chain was slack the whole of its length, and the weight hung an inch clear of the floor, and the lens went on turning.
text_nonnarrative: Rate was the sole criterion of a sound lamp: four revolutions to the minute, no more and no less, whatever the state of the clockwork. Rust on the drive was a matter for the record and not a fault in itself. A slack chain was the one condition that counted against the lens, since weight clear of the floor was the definition of a stopped train, not of a turning one.

text_narrative: Nobody in the shed would work behind Tomos, and there was a reason for it. He took a fleece off in one piece, never two, and he did it faster than the man on the next stand could do it badly. The trouble was the second cuts. He left them all over the board, and the classer had to pick through every fleece he threw, and it cost more time than he saved.
text_nonnarrative: A fleece was classed on the length of its staple and on the proportion of second cuts in it, and the two were independent of each other. Speed at the stand was no part of the class, nor was a fleece off in one piece worth more than a fleece off in two. Second cuts loose on the board were of no account; those bound into the fleece cost the classer time.

text_narrative: Iolanda broke the mould at dawn and the bell came out whole, which was the first thing, and then she saw the line. It ran from the shoulder to the waist, a hair's width, grey against grey. She struck the bell with the heel of her hand and it answered true. She struck it again at the waist, over the line, and the note went flat and stayed flat.
text_nonnarrative: A casting flaw is graded by its depth and its position, never by its length or its width. A grey line at the shoulder is cosmetic, since the shoulder carries little of the vibration. The same line at the waist is disqualifying, because the waist is where the note of a bell is set. Soundness under one strike of the hand is no criterion; what counts is whether the note holds flat.

text_narrative: Maret's third arrow goes into the same hole as her second, which the range master has never seen, and she does not look pleased about it. She nocks the fourth. Behind the target the straw is packed too loose and the shafts are punching clean through into the earth bank. She has lost two heads already this morning. She shoots anyway, and the fourth goes through as well.
text_nonnarrative: A grouping was judged on its diameter alone, and arrows in one hole were counted as a group of nil, which was the highest score available. Loss of a head was a matter for the range's account and never for the score. Shafts through the target were not a fault in the shot; the fault lay in the packing of the straw and in the bank behind it.

text_narrative: The dairy at Kelso had a churn that soured milk in half the time of any other in the district and nobody ever worked out why. They scalded it, they scrubbed it, they took the staves apart one winter and put them back in the same order. Old Bregha said it was the wood and the rest said it was the water, and it went on souring milk for thirty years.
text_nonnarrative: Souring is timed from the set of the curd, not from the first change in smell, and the two are hours apart. A churn is held responsible only where the same milk sours in it and keeps in another of the same wood, and the staves are no part of the question. Water hardness is the commoner cause, since it acts on every vessel in a district rather than on one.

text_narrative: Ferran finds the thermal by the crows and not by the instrument, which is a second behind him the whole way. He banks hard left and holds thirty degrees. The variometer catches up, reads four metres up, then two, then nothing at all, and he is out the far side of it before the needle has settled. He comes round again on the same crows.
text_nonnarrative: A thermal was reckoned found where lift held for a full turn, and a single reading in metres was not sufficient. Instrument lag was allowed for by discounting the first seconds of any indication, the needle being slower than the air. Crows were evidence of a core, not of its strength, and a bank angle beyond thirty degrees was held to lose more in drag than it gained.

text_narrative: There was a keep whose walls were held by four ward-stones, and the youngest daughter of the house was set to read them each Michaelmas. Three she found sound. The fourth had gone the colour of wet ash at the seam and rang hollow under her knuckle, and she wrote it down as sound, because the mason who had cut it was her father, and she was fifteen.
text_nonnarrative: A ward-stone was read at the seam and nowhere else, colour first and tone second. Ash-grey at the seam was the sole disqualifying colour; every other shade was permitted whatever its depth. A hollow tone was corroborating and never sufficient on its own, since tone was a property of the mounting as much as of the stone, and a sound stone badly set rang hollow too.

text_narrative: Adaeze is nine hours into the survey and the pitting on panel forty is not what the manifest says it should be. The holes are round. Every other panel on the ship shows the long grazes of a glancing strike, and forty is punched clean through in nine places, front to back, as though something had come at it square. She marks it and moves to forty-one.
text_nonnarrative: Pitting was classed by the ratio of depth to width, and a round hole and a long graze were separate classes with separate tolerances. Count was secondary to class, and the manifest count secondary again. Penetration front to back was disqualifying in either class, whatever the count, since the criterion was the integrity of the panel rather than the number of strikes on its face.

text_narrative: The society's fourth secretary was a man named Bosch who had never seen anything and did not expect to. He filed reports for nine years. In the tenth he sat up with a lamp in the east corridor of a house in Ghent, and at two he wrote a line in the register and closed it, and he resigned the following week without adding to the entry.
text_nonnarrative: A report is admitted to the society's register on the number of independent witnesses and on the interval between the sighting and the entry, and on nothing else. A single witness is admissible where the interval is under an hour. Length is no criterion; a line filed at the hour carries the weight of a full account, and an account a week later carries none. The secretary holds both.

text_narrative: Vasile walked the up line from the viaduct to the tunnel mouth every Tuesday for twenty-two years. On the last Tuesday he found the gauge wide by nine millimetres over four sleepers, and the keys sound, and the chairs sound, and no reason for it anywhere he could see. He packed the ballast, wrote it in the book, and walked back to look at it again before dark.
text_nonnarrative: Gauge is a fault at a threshold rather than by degree: nine millimetres wide over four sleepers is within tolerance on straight track and outside it on any curve. Soundness of keys and chairs bears on the cause and not on the classification. Ballast is a remedy for a subsiding fault and no remedy where keys and chairs are sound, since the widening then lies in the rail itself.

text_narrative: Marku kept eleven hives on the south wall and the ninth swarmed twice in one summer, which he took as an insult. He opened it in July and there was brood in every frame and no queen anywhere in it. He shut it again. In August it swarmed a third time, and when he opened it that evening there were two queens on the same comb, and neither would fight.
text_nonnarrative: Queenlessness was read from the brood and not from the temper of a hive, and brood of all ages in every frame was sufficient evidence of a laying queen whether one was seen or not. A hive opened in July and again in August gave two readings of one condition. Two queens on one comb were classed as a supersedure rather than a swarm, and were left alone.

text_narrative: Aurel finds the fault on the third pick. One warp thread is riding above the heddle eye instead of through it, and every shed since has closed on it, so the cloth carries a float four rows deep. He stops the loom mid-beat. He does not unpick yet; he leans in and follows the thread back along the warp to the beam, looking for where it left its eye.
text_nonnarrative: On a countermarch loom the shed was the interval between the lifted and the unlifted warp, and every thread's position in it was fixed by the eye of one heddle. A float was a length of warp outside that control, unbound on the face of the cloth. Its depth in rows was a measure of the number of picks affected, not of the severity of the fault.

text_narrative: Ilse pulled the great open diapason at the end of the voluntary and the whole west end of the church went out of tune at once. She held it. Four pipes in the middle of the rank were a quarter-tone flat together, which was not damp and not dust, and she knew the sound of both. She finished on the flutes and went up into the loft with a lamp.
text_nonnarrative: A rank of pipes is fed from one wind-chest through a single slider, and its pitch is a function of the pressure in that chest and of the length of each pipe. A run of adjacent pipes flat by an equal interval is a property of the chest, since dust and damp are local to the pipe and give scattered rather than adjacent deviation across a rank.

text_narrative: Nen has the case open and the movement face down on the pad and the escapement is doing something no escapement does. The balance turns one way. It has turned one way for six hours by the wall clock, never back, and the hairspring is neither wound nor slack. Under the loupe the pallet jewels are not touching the escape wheel at all, and the wheel is turning too.
text_nonnarrative: In a lever escapement the balance was coupled to the escape wheel through two pallet jewels, and its motion was necessarily reciprocal: each impulse was the release of one tooth and the locking of the next. The hairspring was the return element and set the period. Contact between pallet and wheel was the whole of the coupling, and without it the balance and the wheel were independent bodies of independent period.

text_narrative: The mill above Sarvar turned its cap into the wind on the fifth of every month whatever the wind was doing, and the miller's son sat under the fantail one November to watch it happen. The fantail was still. The cap came round anyway, forty degrees against the wind, and settled, and the sails began to turn backwards and grind as well as they ever had.
text_nonnarrative: The cap of a tower mill was carried on a curb of rollers and was turned by a fantail geared down to a worm on the curb. The fantail was the sole source of that motion and stood at right angles to the sails, so that any wind across the cap was its drive. With the fantail at rest the cap and the wind were in a fixed relation.

text_narrative: The press at Trencsen had a platen that came down true on the left and shy on the right by the thickness of a card, and every apprentice was told about it on the first day. They packed the tympan under the right side and it printed clean for forty years. When the frame was finally trued in ninety-one the packing stayed in, and it printed shy on the left.
text_nonnarrative: Impression on a hand press is a function of the parallelism between platen and bed, and is adjusted at the tympan rather than at the frame. Packing under one side of the tympan is a rise on that side of the thickness of the packing. The correction is therefore a property of the packing and not of the platen, and is specific to the frame it fits.

text_narrative: The ring is at eight-tenths of a gravity and Oyeyemi is standing in the spoke access with a wrench she has no use for, listening. There is a beat in it. Once a revolution something in the outboard bearing takes up and lets go, and the whole ring steps a hand's width out of true and steps back, and the gauges on the hub read nothing at all.
text_nonnarrative: A habitation ring was supported at the hub on a single bearing race and was stiff only in the plane of rotation. Displacement out of that plane was resisted by the spokes in tension and was therefore periodic at the rotation frequency wherever any one spoke was slack. Hub instruments were referenced to the hub and were insensitive to displacement of the rim at any frequency.

text_narrative: A duke had an automaton that wrote his name in a fair hand, and he showed it to every visitor for eleven years. In the twelfth a girl who cleaned the room noticed that it wrote the name in a different hand on Sundays, smaller and sloped the other way, and that nobody wound it on Saturday nights, and that it wrote on Sundays all the same.
text_nonnarrative: A writing automaton stored its text as a cam stack, one cam to each stroke, and the hand it produced was a property of the cam profiles rather than of the mechanism that read them. Selection between stacks was by a lever at the base. The mainspring was the sole source of power, and its state of wind bore on speed alone and not on legibility.

text_narrative: Brona worked the bottom lock at Ardara for nine seasons and never had a chamber empty in under four minutes until the March the culvert silted. That morning it took eleven. She raised the paddles full and stood on the beam and watched the water come down the wall in a thin sheet instead of a boil, and the level in the chamber hardly moved at all.
text_nonnarrative: A lock empties through culverts in the chamber wall, and the rate is set by the smallest cross-section anywhere in that path rather than by the opening of the paddles. Full paddle travel is therefore no guarantee of full flow. Sheet discharge at the wall face rather than turbulence is a property of low velocity, and low velocity in a fixed culvert is a matter of obstruction.

text_narrative: Second service and the pass is backed up four plates. Ivo has the tongs in his left hand and is holding a sauce spoon in his teeth because both burners went at once. He sets down the halibut, wipes the rim with his thumb, and sees the sauce has broken — a grey ring already spreading at the edge of the plate. He calls for a new plate and starts again.
text_nonnarrative: An emulsion differs from a suspension in what holds the two phases apart: in the first, a film at the interface; in the second, nothing but the viscosity of the medium. Broken and split are not synonyms. A broken sauce is one without the film, separated by density, grey at the rim and clear beneath. A split one is intact but over-thinned, an error of proportion rather than of technique.

text_narrative: There was a cellarman at Vouvray who could name a fault in a glass before it reached his mouth and was wrong about one bottle in his life. It was a magnum from ninety-four and he called it cork across the room. They opened it and the cork was sound as a bell. He drank a glass, said nothing, and never called a fault from across a room again.
text_nonnarrative: Cork taint differs from oxidation in what it removes rather than in what it adds: the first mutes fruit and leaves the structure intact, the second flattens the structure and leaves an apple note in its place. Reduction is a third and separate class, distinguished from both by its reversibility in air. None of the three is diagnosable from the state of the cork itself, nor from its age.

text_narrative: The Hesperine carried nine miles of cordage and one length of it would not take a splice. Kovac tried it four times off Cadiz and the lay opened every time within a fathom of the join. On the fifth he laid it up over a thimble instead and it held to the end of the voyage, and it held when they tested it to breaking in Lisbon at twice its rated load.
text_nonnarrative: A splice differs from a knot in that it is made within the lay of the rope and not around it, so a splice is a property of the rope's construction and a knot is a property of its path. A hitch is a third class, distinguished from both by requiring a second object. Only the first of the three is sensitive to the lay, and only the first is permanent.

text_narrative: The physician at Ravensmoor kept a chart of the sick with three columns and by the second week she had drawn a fourth. The new column had two names in it. Both had the flush and the tremor of the second column and neither had the fever, and both were sitting up and talking on the ninth day, and everyone in the second column was gone by the seventh.
text_nonnarrative: The three classes are distinguished by which signs occur together, not by severity. Flush with fever is the first class; tremor with fever is the second. Flush and tremor without fever belong to neither, and are a fourth class rather than a mild form of the second, since the ninth day is the point of divergence and mildness alone would not produce a divergence of that kind.

text_narrative: A smith in the hills graded her steel in four names and sold the third for the price of the first, and no lord who bought it ever complained. Her daughter asked why. She said the fourth grade broke, and the first grade held, and the second and third both held, and only one man in a hundred could tell the second from the third, and none of them bought steel.
text_nonnarrative: The four grades were distinguished by carbon and by the evenness of its distribution, and not by hardness, which was a property of the finished blade. The first and second differed in evenness alone. The third was even but low in carbon, and the fourth was uneven and high, which was the one combination without toughness at any temper, and the only one of the four beyond correction.

text_narrative: Ilinca has the barometer on the sill and the barometer says nothing has changed since Tuesday. The sky says otherwise. There is a sheet of grey over the whole valley with a hole in it directly above the house, a clean-edged hole about a mile across, and inside the hole the air is perfectly clear, and the sheet has not moved in either direction for two days.
text_nonnarrative: Stratus differs from altostratus in altitude and in edge: the lower sheet is diffuse at its margins, the higher one sharp enough to cast a defined shadow. Both are layer forms and neither is a convective form. A hole in a layer form is classed by its edge rather than by its size, since a sharp edge belongs to subsidence and a ragged one to erosion.

text_narrative: The tide was out past the second bar when Marek saw the boat, and it was coming in without a wake. He watched it cross water too shallow to float it. When it grounded, nothing stepped off. He walked down to the hull and found it dry to the touch, dry inside, dry along the keel where it had come up through six feet of sea, and warm.
text_nonnarrative: Three bars lie parallel to the shingle, the outermost above water only at the lowest tides. Between the second bar and the shore the depth at slack is under two feet, too little for a keeled hull, and the bed is firm sand rather than mud. The landward side of each bar is the drier of the two, and the whole foreshore is above the waterline for six hours in twelve.

text_narrative: Anselm surveyed the Bruckner system for three summers and in the third he found the chamber. It was four hundred metres in and eighty metres across and the floor was flat, flat as a threshing floor, and dry. There was no sediment anywhere in it and no formation on the walls, and his tape gave him the same reading in every direction from the centre, to the centimetre.
text_nonnarrative: The system is three levels of passage on a single joint set, with the lowest at four hundred metres from the entrance and the largest chambers on it. Floors are sediment over breakdown and are level only in the last hundred metres. Chamber plans are elongate along the joint rather than circular, and wall formation is general below the second level and absent above it.

text_narrative: They used to say the pass at Dovre was open on the ninth of May and shut on the ninth of October and a man could set his year by it. Nobody says it now. The winter Lisbet drove the mail over it she went up on the second of May on bare stone and came back on the twenty-eighth through four feet of new snow, and it was the same year both times.
text_nonnarrative: The pass lies at nine hundred metres on a north-south axis, with the steeper ground on the northern approach and a broad saddle at the summit. The saddle itself is level for some six hundred metres. Snow lies longest in the eastern hollows below it, which are in shadow from October. The southern approach is stone for most of its length and holds no great depth of snow at any season.

text_narrative: Urena is eleven kilometres out on the flat and the tracks behind her are the only marks on it in any direction. Ahead of her there is a line. It runs east and west as far as she can see, a hand's width wide, and it is not a crack and not a ridge, and when she kneels and puts her glove on it the salt is warm, and everywhere else it is not.
text_nonnarrative: The flat was a hundred and forty kilometres across and lay within two metres of level over its whole extent. Relief across it was nowhere abrupt. The surface was a salt crust of some centimetres over brine. Lineations were general and ran east and west, at intervals of a few kilometres, and were expressed as differences in crust temperature rather than in relief, and were visible only as differences in tone.

text_narrative: Kwabena mapped the delta twice, in the dry and in the flood, and the two maps did not agree about the third channel. In the dry it ran south-east to the sea. In the flood it ran south-west, the same channel, the same banks, and the water in it going the other way round the same island, and the island in both maps exactly where it had been.
text_nonnarrative: The delta was seven channels on a fan of some thirty kilometres, of which the third was the deepest and the least confined by levees. Bed gradients across the fan were under a metre in ten kilometres. At that gradient the direction of any channel was a function of stage rather than of relief, and the islands between channels were stable in position at all stages.

text_narrative: There was a fen that gave up one thing a year and always in the same month, and the men of the two villages that bordered it drew lots for the finding. In the year of the great drought it gave up a boat with a mast, standing upright in the peat with its sail set, forty miles from any water that would float it, and the sail was dry.
text_nonnarrative: The fen was some nine thousand hectares of peat over clay, with the peat at four to six metres through the centre and thinner at both margins. Water table stood within a foot of the surface for most of the year. Objects within the peat were at all depths and in all attitudes, and the peat was anaerobic throughout, so preservation was general rather than local to any part.

text_narrative: Everyone at that school remembers the year the bell broke. It rang at eleven twenty instead of noon, every day, for a fortnight, and nobody in the office would admit to knowing why. Half the school ate lunch early. The other half sat through forty extra minutes of double maths because their teacher refused to go by anything but her own watch, and she was right, and it didn't help.
text_nonnarrative: Reported lunch timing varies more within schools than between them. In the sample, 46 percent of pupils take lunch inside a twenty-minute window around noon; the rest are distributed across the forty minutes on either side. Teacher-held timing accounts for most of the spread: where a class follows a clock other than the bell, its lunch start sits a mean eighteen minutes from the school median, in either direction.

text_narrative: The inspector for the fourth district was a woman called Wieczorek and she walked every stair in it in the spring of the year the census came round. At number nine Krochmalna she counted eleven in the front room and wrote it down and knocked on the back. The back room had one man in it, and a bed, and four chairs set round the walls, and he was paying twice the front room's rent.
text_nonnarrative: Occupancy per room varies more between rooms in one building than between buildings in one district. In the fourth district the median is four persons to a room, with a quarter of rooms above eight and a tenth below two. Building age accounts for none of the variance in either measure. Rent per room is uncorrelated with occupancy and correlated with position, front rooms being the cheaper at every level of occupancy.

text_narrative: The screen is up and the panel has heard nine cellists and the ninth is playing the same passage the fourth played. Note for note, breath for breath, down to a lift before the last phrase that is not in the part. Somoza looks at the list. The fourth candidate withdrew before the audition began and her name is struck through in his own hand.
text_nonnarrative: Behind a screen the distribution of panel scores was about a fifth narrower than the same panel's scoring in view. Agreement between panellists was highest at the extremes and lowest in the third quartile, where a third of all placings were decided. Order of appearance accounted for a mean of two places, candidates heard late in a session placing higher than their scores alone would give.

text_narrative: Rahim kept the arrivals book at the north quay for nineteen years and in the last of them he began to keep a second book of his own. In the second book he wrote down what the men said their trades were and what they were doing a month later. Of the hundred and forty joiners in the first year, three were joining wood. The rest were on the coal.
text_nonnarrative: Declared trade and trade at one month agreed in about a fifth of returns. Declaration itself was made once and was never revised. Agreement was highest among trades with a licensing requirement and lowest among the building trades, of which joinery was the largest single declaration. Coal handling was the destination of a third of all arrivals, and was itself declared by fewer than one man in fifty.

text_narrative: Berth allocation closes at midnight and Tsegay has four hundred and six names for four hundred berths and no way to choose between them. He runs the lottery. It gives him four hundred names and the six it leaves out are the six who were last on the list, in order, which a lottery does not do. He runs it again with a new seed and it gives him the same six.
text_nonnarrative: Allocation by lottery gave a uniform distribution over list position, with departures from uniformity of the order of the square root of the count. At four hundred and six names the expected number of the final six excluded by chance was under a tenth. Repeated draws under independent seeds were independent, and agreement between two draws on the excluded set was a matter of one in some millions of draws.

text_narrative: Everybody on the Thursday market knew that Aunty Fetuma's stall took more money on a wet day than a dry one and everybody had a theory about it. She had the corner under the arch. When they roofed the whole market in seventy-eight and there was no wet and no dry any more, her takings settled at the wet-day figure and stayed there, and the theories stopped.
text_nonnarrative: Takings per stall vary with position more than with weather, and the two are confounded where shelter is unevenly distributed. Corner pitches under permanent cover show a coefficient of variation across weather of under a tenth; open pitches show four times that. Under a roof the open pitches sit at the level of the covered ones, and the difference between the classes is small at all weathers.

text_narrative: There was a miller who owed the river a debt and paid it in flour, a handful thrown from the sluice gate every Friday at dusk. For nine years the wheel turned in drought and in flood alike. In the tenth year he kept the handful back, and the water rose to the axle and stopped there, neither turning the wheel nor falling, and it waited.
text_nonnarrative: A breastshot wheel takes water at about axle height, between the overshot and undershot arrangements, and converts both the weight and the impulse of the flow. Its efficiency depends on the sluice gate, which sets the depth of water admitted to the buckets. Head above the axle is wasted; head below it does not fill the buckets. The working range is therefore narrow and fixed by the gate.

text_narrative: The eclipse was due at four minutes past eleven and at four minutes past eleven it came, and Halvorsen had his plate exposed and his watch in his hand. Totality ran two minutes and eleven seconds, as predicted. Then it ran again. The shadow came back over the same ground in the same direction eleven minutes later and lasted the same two minutes and eleven seconds, and no almanac had it.
text_nonnarrative: A total eclipse is the passage of the lunar umbra across the surface, and its duration at any point is a function of the umbral diameter there and of the relative velocity of the shadow. Both are set by the orbits alone. The umbra is single and its track is monotonic in longitude, so any point on the surface lies within it for one interval only in a given syzygy.

text_narrative: Sigrun cut turf on the same bank as her mother and her mother's mother and in the summer of the bad hay she cut down to something at seven feet. It was a hand, and a wrist, and a sleeve of woven stuff with a red thread in it, and the red was as red as the day it was dyed, and the fingernails were clean and cut short.
text_nonnarrative: Peat was the accumulation of plant matter under waterlogged and acid conditions, at rates of the order of a millimetre in a year, so that depth was a proxy for age. The same conditions were hostile to bacterial action and to most fading. Organic material within the peat was therefore subject to compression and to staining rather than to decay, at any depth in the bank.

text_narrative: Mireia is on the wall an hour before the bore and the water below her is going out, which is right, and then it stops. It does not turn. It stands still the whole width of the channel for a count of two hundred, flat as a table and level with the mark, and then it goes on out again, and the bore comes up on time behind it.
text_nonnarrative: A tidal bore was the front of the flood tide propagating into a converging channel against the ebb, and required a large range, a shallow bed and a narrowing plan. Its arrival was set by the tide and not by the state of the ebb before it. Slack water was the interval of zero mean velocity and was of the order of minutes in such channels.

text_narrative: The herald has the roll open at the fourth quarter and the fourth quarter is wrong. It bears three martlets where the roll of ninety years back bears two, and the roll of forty years back bears two, and the paint over the third is the same age as the paint under it. Nobody has added a martlet. He turns the page and the arms opposite bear four.
text_nonnarrative: Charges were counted as part of the blazon and were not subject to variation at the painter's discretion, so a difference in number between two rolls was a difference in the arms borne. Marshalling by quarters placed a distinct coat in each quarter. Cadency was expressed by an added mark rather than by an altered count, which made the count the more stable element of a blazon.

text_narrative: Nadia is three lifts up when the board under her right foot gives half an inch and stops. She does not move. She looks down through the gap at the coupler holding the ledger and sees it is a right-angle clamp where a swivel should be, and that whoever set it has run the bolt in from the wrong side, so the jaw is open toward the load. She whistles once.
text_nonnarrative: Ledger connections were required to be made with right-angle couplers, swivel couplers being permitted only where a member met another out of square. Bolts were to be entered from the side away from the load, so that the jaw was closed against it rather than open toward it. Boards were to bear on three supports, with no unsupported span admitting vertical movement greater than a quarter inch at any lift.

text_narrative: The inspector came to Halim's bakery every quarter for eleven years and every quarter the loaves were four grams over and he wrote it down as compliant. In the twelfth year a new inspector came and weighed nine loaves and found them four grams over, and asked why, and Halim said because the old man liked them four grams over. She wrote that down too.
text_nonnarrative: A loaf sold by weight is required to be not less than its declared weight, with no upper limit imposed by the schedule. Compliance is determined on the mean of a stated number of units and not on any single unit. A shortfall in one unit within a compliant mean is not an offence, and a uniform excess is outside the scope of the schedule entirely.

text_narrative: The Coriander went down in eleven minutes in flat calm and every soul aboard her was taken off in the boats, which was not what the inquiry expected to find. The second officer had swung all four davits out at the first alarm, before the order, against standing instructions, and had been reprimanded twice that year for doing the same thing in drills.
text_nonnarrative: Davits were required to be capable of turning out a fully loaded boat with the ship listed fifteen degrees either way, and the turning out was to be effected by the falls alone without recourse to power. Boats were to be kept inboard except as the master directed. That direction was a condition of the requirement and not a matter of the davit's capability.

text_narrative: There was a guild that bound its apprentices for seven years and one day, and a boy came to it who had already served six years to a master in another town. They argued it a whole winter. In the end they bound him for seven years and one day and set him to the work of a journeyman from the first morning, and paid him nothing, and he stayed.
text_nonnarrative: Articles were to run for a term of seven years and one day from the date of binding, and prior service elsewhere was not to be set against the term. Work assigned was at the discretion of the master and was not required to correspond to the stage of the term. Maintenance was the master's obligation; wages were not within the articles at any stage of it.

text_narrative: The reading room had been sealed for two hundred years and the air inside still moved. Oyelaran set the lamp on the nearest table and the dust did not lift. It hung where it was, in layers, each one flat and separate, as though something had been turning the room over slowly all that time and had stopped only when the door opened. The catalogue drawers were warm.
text_nonnarrative: Sealing a collection preserves the object and forfeits the reason for keeping it. The argument for closed storage rests on rates of decay, which are real and well measured; the argument against rests on use, which is harder to quantify and so tends to lose. But a catalogue no one opens is not a lesser holding than one in circulation. It is a different thing, and its decay is not material.

text_narrative: The crate stood in the basement at Leiden for sixty years with a number on it and nothing else, and when Adjoa finally opened it in the spring there were two of everything inside. Two masks, two staffs, two of the small bronze figures, each pair identical to the eye, each pair with one label. The register had a single entry, dated 1898, and the word duplicate in a later hand.
text_nonnarrative: The case for return rests on provenance, and provenance is precisely what a poorly kept register destroys. That is an argument for return rather than against it. A museum unable to say how an object came to it is in no position to claim that it came lawfully, and the burden of a missing record properly falls on the party whose duty it was to keep one in the first place.

text_narrative: There was a schoolmistress in the valley who fined her pupils a penny for every word of the dialect and kept the pennies in a jar on her desk. At the end of the year she bought a dictionary with them. She read out of it to the class every Friday for the rest of her life, and every one of those children spoke the dialect at home until they died.
text_nonnarrative: A standard is useful in proportion to the number of people it reaches, and a dialect is useful in proportion to how well it fits the life of the people who speak it. These are different goods and neither displaces the other. The case for teaching the standard is therefore not a case against the dialect, and schooling that treats it as one loses both of them at the same time.
